correctness.rationale: For any fixed \(p\in(0,1)\), the product Bernoulli stationary law and entry flux \(\mu_n=p(1-p)^n\) follow by exact coordinate refresh. The visited-set identity \(a_{r+1}=p\,\mathbb E[q^{K_r}W_r]\) is derived conditional on coordinate indices, and exact-rational state propagation independently checks this identity in finite dimensions. When \(w_+=O(n^{-\gamma})\), repeat-index subset bounds imply \(\sum_{j\le b_n}a_j=o(1)\); this controls the second factorial moment of stationary block entrances. With \(w_-\ge c n^{-B}\), coupling after all coordinates update gives \(\alpha_n(h_n)=o(b_n\mu_n)\), and an empty-start union bound gives negligible burn-in hits. Stationary rare-entry blocks separated by mixing gaps yield the exponential hitting law; a uniform block success bound provides uniform exponential tails and convergence of all fixed moments. Finally, selection of an exponentially rare required coordinate bounds the entire completion probability and proves the obstruction. The asymptotic proof is analytical; 540 finite assertions are not substituted for infinitely many parameter cases.

originality.rationale: Attrill–Garoni (arXiv:2605.14206v1) and Long (arXiv:2605.14511v1, Section 4) study a uniformly selected coupon; Long establishes the existing stationary flux and general block criterion. The present specific theorem permits arbitrary polynomially diffuse unequal selection frequencies, proves a visited-set clumping estimate without the uniform birth–death count chain, and gives the exponentially rare-coordinate obstruction. Long Section 3.6 handles nonuniform coupon draws only for the mechanically different global reset-button collector. Cruciani–Dudeja (arXiv:2602.20705v1) globally thins held coupons, also a different chain. Searches for equivalent rare random-scan product-chain statements found no explicit covering theorem; this absence is evidence-limited rather than a proof of priority.
residual_risks: An earlier theorem for inhomogeneous random-scan heat-bath chains might cover the all-profile limit as an unstated corollary; no exhaustive priority certification is claimed.
The closest separately published nonuniform reset-coupon record was available only as a summary, not a fully read proof; its described process is different.
The main fixed-probability uniform law and the generic rare-entry theorem are both already known and explicitly excluded from novelty claims.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by the existing fixed-loss clumsy collector and asks whether strongly unequal, including Zipf, coupon frequencies alter its exponentially rare completion clock. The result exhibits a whole family of genuinely nonuniform arrival laws with one universal entry-scale and complete moment limits; its set-of-refreshed-coordinates estimate replaces a one-dimensional Markov reduction that breaks under unequal sampling. The explicit exponentially rare-coordinate family breaks the law on the same scaling, delimiting the meaningful range of universality. This is a structural frequency-class result rather than a fixed-size enumeration or a routine restatement of the uniform theorem.
